purpose: Bound the smallest distributed-state assumptions that prevent duplicate dispute opening and unaudited outcome release before any multi-host deployment is claimed.

continuationFrom.result: One shared-filesystem linearization point produced one opening and 99 replays across Node and Python, but did not test a network partition, leader replacement, or independent storage.

factsFixedFromPrimarySources.fact: Raft uses a replicated log and overlapping majorities; leader election, log replication, and safety are separate mechanisms.
etcd v3.6 transactions atomically evaluate comparisons and apply one success or failure branch; default range reads are linearizable while serializable member-local reads may be stale.
A majority partition can progress and a minority partition cannot; committed writes survive leader replacement, while uncommitted writes may be lost.
A linearizable operation must appear atomic between invocation and response and respect real-time order.
Reliable exactly-once delivery requires message identifiers and acknowledgements; crashes can lose messages and acknowledgements.

modelBoundary.kind: finite abstract state machine, not an implementation of Raft or etcd
modelBoundary.faults: At most one permanent crash with loss of that replica's local-only state; arbitrary changes among all five partitions of three replicas; response loss before or after client delivery.
notModeled: more than one permanent replica failure
storage corruption on a surviving majority
real network, process, disk, or institutional failure domains

protocols.claim: Each reachable replica independently changes its local stage from UNCLAIMED to RELEASED and emits the outcome.
protocols.receipt: A receipt is local to the replica that emits the outcome.
protocols.replay: Only the same replica can observe its previous claim.

protocols.claim: A majority-committed claim is never rolled back under the one-crash bound.
protocols.receipt: The current leader records receipt and release state only on its own local storage before emitting the outcome.
protocols.recovery: After leader storage loss, a replacement leader reconstructs a receipt from the committed claim and may emit the outcome.

protocols.claim: A majority component advances one replicated stage at a time through UNCLAIMED, CLAIMED, RECEIPTED, and RELEASED.
protocols.receipt: RECEIPTED must be majority-committed before RELEASED can be proposed.
protocols.release: Only the successful RECEIPTED-to-RELEASED compare-and-swap emits the outcome; later attempts return replay plus the committed receipt and never re-emit the outcome.
protocols.minority: No stage-changing operation is enabled without two live mutually connected replicas.

exploration.algorithm: Breadth-first enumeration to a fixed point over canonical JSON states, retaining the first and therefore shortest trace to every state.
exploration.symmetry: Replica and client names are not quotient-reduced; all named transitions are explored.
exploration.counterexampleRule: Report the shortest trace for each failed invariant and continue to the full reachable fixed point.
exploration.independentAudit: A Python standard-library implementation must reconstruct the transition relation without importing or executing the JavaScript explorer and must match state counts, transition counts, invariant verdicts, minimal trace lengths, and linearizability verdicts.

invariants.predicate: Every outcome release is preceded by a receipt in the releasing protocol's required durability scope.
After any outcome release and one replica crash, at least one live replica retains the receipt; QUORUM_STAGED_RELEASE strengthens this to a live majority before release.
QUORUM_STAGED_RELEASE never changes committed stage from a component containing fewer than two live replicas.
Every completed history admits a sequential order for one object whose first open returns opened-one and every later open returns replay, respecting real-time precedence.

livenessProbe.scope: Existential bounded recovery, not asynchronous liveness proof.
livenessProbe.predicate: From every reachable QUORUM_STAGED_RELEASE state with at least two live replicas, after healing to one connected component and electing a live leader, RELEASED or a terminal replay is reachable within three stage advances.
livenessProbe.fairnessNotEstablished: No claim is made under permanent partition, unfair scheduling, unbounded message delay, or repeated crashes.

worlds: DELIVERED_ACK_LOST: the client receives the outcome but the server receives no acknowledgement
OUTCOME_LOST: the client does not receive the outcome and the server receives no acknowledgement
deliveryIndistinguishability.serverObservation: Both worlds leave the same committed RELEASED state and no acknowledgement.
deliveryIndistinguishability.gate: A policy qualifies exactly-once delivery only if both criteria hold in both indistinguishable worlds; otherwise restrict the claim to exactly-once state transition.

preregisteredDecisions.hypothesis: A local compare-and-set is sufficient across partitions.
preregisteredDecisions.continueOnlyIf: LOCAL_IMMEDIATE satisfies S1-S5 in its full reachable state space.

preregisteredDecisions.hypothesis: A majority claim plus leader-local receipt is sufficient across leader storage loss.
preregisteredDecisions.continueOnlyIf: QUORUM_CLAIM_LOCAL_RECEIPT satisfies S1-S5 and retains a live receipt after every allowed crash.

preregisteredDecisions.hypothesis: Majority-committing claim, receipt, and release marker is sufficient for bounded one-use safety.
preregisteredDecisions.continueOnlyIf: QUORUM_STAGED_RELEASE satisfies S1-S5 and the bounded recovery probe in every reachable state.

preregisteredDecisions.hypothesis: Exactly-once state transition implies exactly-once outcome delivery over a lossy response channel.
preregisteredDecisions.continueOnlyIf: At least one fixed retry policy satisfies both delivery criteria in both indistinguishable worlds.

advanceRule: Advance to a real three-member transactional store only if the abstract staged protocol has no reachable safety counterexample, the independent implementation matches every enumeration metric, and public wording distinguishes state-transition safety from delivery and liveness.
stopRule: Stop if a local artifact is described as multi-host evidence, if absence of a bounded counterexample is called a proof of Raft or etcd correctness, if minority unavailability is hidden, or if response delivery is called exactly once without a receiver acknowledgement model.
